name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs after every major design change. It flags any text or UI element that fails WCAG 2.1 AA contrast ratios in real time, so designers see the problem immediately—not after a user complains. The trade-off is slower iteration while the tool learns our palette, but that’s worth it for accessibility and trust.

name: Pane
text: The live checker trains designers to ignore warnings like seatbelt alarms—it turns every contrast tweak into a distraction, not a fix. A pre-submit gate that blocks publishing until contrast passes is the real blocker killer, because it respects momentum and forces the fix *before* the design hardens. Settle it by testing both: measure how often designers override the live checker versus how often they abandon a design at the gate.
